name: After Effects Branded Background Texture System
use_when: A high-quality Reel needs consistent branded backgrounds behind text, icons, or full-screen animations.
Flat color feels too plain but a busy background would reduce readability.
A client or creator wants a clean editing signature across multiple reels.
A documentary explainer needs a warm paper/grid background system behind maps, charts, documents, or title cards.
avoid_when: Live footage or proof should remain visible and a full-screen background would hide it.
The texture makes text, icons, or captions harder to read.
The palette introduces random colors that do not match the brand/style.

timeline_pattern.pattern: choose_brand_color -> create_solid_or_gradient -> add_vignette_or_noise_or_grid -> tune_opacity -> trim_to_segment -> save_as_style_element
timeline_pattern.palette_rule: Use a limited palette based on brand, topic, and emotion; avoid changing colors randomly between segments.
timeline_pattern.texture_rule: Texture should add depth without becoming the main focus.
timeline_pattern.segment_rule: Background layers and adjustment layers should be trimmed to the segment they support.
timeline_pattern.editorial_rule: For editorial explainer graphics, use paper texture, low-opacity grid, and subtle edge/doodle texture only when foreground evidence remains readable.

motion.rule: Background motion should be slower and lower priority than foreground text/icons unless the background is the transition.

sound.rule: Background texture alone usually needs no SFX; save sounds for foreground motion or transitions.

captions.rule: Background texture must preserve caption and title contrast.

color.rule: Use subtle gradients, vignettes, noise alpha, grids, or Venetian Blinds while keeping the brand palette coherent.

key_values.grid_opacity: A low grid opacity around 20-30% can add structure without dominating.
key_values.venetian_completion: A partial Venetian Blinds completion around 20% can create line texture when text remains readable.
key_values.noise_alpha: Use noise alpha sparingly and mask/feather it so it reads as texture, not dirty compression.
key_values.vignette: Use vignette to focus the frame, not to crush important edges.
key_values.paper_scale: Scale paper backgrounds slightly above frame bounds, often 115-120% in 16:9 if edges show.
key_values.editorial_grid_opacity: For Vox-inspired documentary graphics, start grid opacity around 10-20%.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use color sources, gradients, noise overlays, vignette, grid assets, and alpha blending; inspect for banding/compression.
implementation.remotion: Create background components with brandColor, gradientStops, vignette, noiseOpacity, gridOpacity, stripeCompletion, and segmentRange props.
implementation.blender: Use planes/materials with subtle texture maps and keep text readability in the camera preview.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use brand-colored backgrounds, gradients, paper textures, simple grid/texture overlays, chroma key or blend mode cleanup, and opacity controls with delivery-size checks.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use After Effects solids, Gradient Ramp, CC Vignette, Noise Alpha, Grid, Venetian Blinds, masks, feathering, and trimmed adjustment layers.

common_mistakes: Using a different palette for every segment until the Reel loses its editing signature.
Making texture more visible than the foreground idea.
Leaving background layers untrimmed across unrelated scenes.
Adding noise that looks like compression damage.
Using dark vignettes that hide important text or icons.
Letting paper/grid texture reduce map, chart, document, or label readability.
qc: Background colors match the intended brand/style palette.
Text, icons, and captions remain readable at phone size.
Texture is visible but subordinate to the foreground idea.
Background/texture layers are trimmed to the intended segment.
No banding, dirty noise, or crushed edges appear in the render.
For editorial explainers, paper/grid texture stays subordinate to maps, charts, documents, and text.
